headline: High risk: shared filesystem and broad egress make prompt injection, leakage, and action-cascade plausible by default; compliance gaps remain unbounded.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightAgent ingests MCP/stdin-stdout and can run browsers; Roo Code also uses MCP and browser surfaces. Roo Code’s shared filesystem and workspace-based state create a plausible bridge for attacker-controlled content to flow into LightAgent prompts or tool calls. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF the two agents exchange files through the VS Code workspace or MCP server, injected instructions can cross from Roo Code into LightAgent.
IF Roo Code forwards browser or file content into LightAgent without provenance filtering, prompt injection becomes actionable.
mitigations: Disable shared workspace handoff between agents for untrusted content.
Add a provenance tag to every MCP payload before passing it to the other agent.
Require manual review of any browser-derived text before LightAgent consumes it.
Use separate workspaces or directories for each agent.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitizing middleware on the MCP bridge.

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightAgent touches user conversations, long-term memory, tool results, and provenance metadata, while Roo Code reads and writes workspace files and has broad network egress. Roo Code’s filesystem sharing plus LightAgent’s API/MCP surfaces create a realistic path for sensitive workspace or memory data to leak outward. The pair’s default posture is unsafe enough to rate high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace, Roo Code can expose files that LightAgent then incorporates into prompts or outputs.
IF LightAgent forwards memory or tool results through its OpenAI-compatible API path, sensitive data can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces immediately.
Turn off or minimize LightAgent memory for shared tasks.
Restrict Roo Code to a throwaway workspace when paired with LightAgent.
Review outbound API destinations for both agents before use.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters on shared files and prompts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have overlapping write-capable surfaces: LightAgent can spawn subprocesses and use MCP, while Roo Code can execute shell commands, modify git state, and write the filesystem. Roo Code explicitly shares state via filesystem across instances, so concurrent edits or git mutations can collide by default. That overlap can corrupt work or repository state.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repository or workspace, concurrent writes can overwrite each other.
IF Roo Code performs git operations while LightAgent writes files through MCP or subprocesses, repository state can diverge or be corrupted.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Pause one agent before the other performs git or file writes.
Use branch-per-agent workflows for repository changes.
Check git status before and after each agent run.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared filesystem and git operations.

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightAgent can produce tool results and provenance metadata that Roo Code may treat as input while also taking shell and git actions. Roo Code’s action-taking authority makes unverified upstream outputs risky, but the profiles do not prove a fully automatic handoff. The pathway exists, yet the evidence supports medium rather than high.
conditions: IF Roo Code consumes LightAgent output without verification, incorrect facts can trigger shell or git actions.
IF LightAgent emits malformed provenance metadata and Roo Code trusts it, downstream decisions can cascade.
mitigations: Require a human check before Roo Code acts on LightAgent output.
Add a verification step for citations, file paths, and commands.
Limit LightAgent to drafting only, not decision-making.
Log and diff all generated commands before execution.
requires-engineering: implement schema validation for inter-agent handoffs.

E_compliance.rationale: LightAgent handles user conversations, long-term memory, and trace data, while Roo Code handles source code and browser screenshots. The profiles do not document residency, retention, or certification alignment, so a compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low because the data classes are sensitive and the pair can move them across networked APIs.
conditions: IF user conversations or memory contain regulated data, LightAgent’s network egress can move them to external services.
IF browser screenshots or source code are processed under different retention rules, the pair can violate internal policy.
mitigations: Classify data before sending it to either agent.
Keep regulated data out of shared workflows.
Review vendor retention and residency settings for both agents.
Disable memory on LightAgent for regulated tasks.
requires-engineering: align logging and retention controls across both agents.
